answers.children: Harriers are good with children when their energy is matched by active play. Their medium build and playful determination suit romping with older kids but their lively hound exuberance can knock over toddlers during excited pursuits. Bred to hunt hares on foot their stamina keeps them going long after smaller children tire. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Harriers get along with other dogs thanks to their pack-hunting background yet strong prey drive makes them likely to chase smaller pets. Their sociable nature shines in multi-dog homes but the determined scent-tracking instinct can trigger wandering after wildlife. English hound heritage reinforces this chase response over household calm.
answers.exercise: Harriers need one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise such as long hikes or scent games across open ground. Bred for hunting hares by scent their endurance turns to destructive chewing and digging when stimulation falls short. The medium-sized build demands sustained activity rather than brief backyard turns.
answers.shedding: Yes — Harriers shed moderately with short single coats that scatter fine hair around the house. The smooth texture shows dirt easily yet releases it quickly during weekly brushing leaving low grooming demands. Their determined energy means loose hair often appears on furniture after active days outdoors.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and Harriers are not among those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Their short single coat still produces dander and sheds at a moderate level which can affect sensitive individuals. The English hound build offers no special coat qualities that reduce allergens.
answers.training: Harriers are not easy to train because their independent streak and strong prey drive override commands once a scent is detected. Bred for determined hare hunting without constant human direction the medium-sized hound shows moderate intelligence but limited biddability during recall or focus work.
answers.lifespan: Harriers live 12-15 years. Their robust health supports this range in a medium-sized energetic build originally developed for stamina across English countryside. The profile notes no specific vulnerabilities that shorten life yet their need for significant exercise helps maintain condition.
answers.size: Harriers reach 45-60 lb and stand 19-21 in at the shoulder. This compact yet sturdy English hound build feels solid and muscular in the home without overwhelming space. Proportions allow the determined energy of scent-tracking to be contained in a medium frame suited to foot hunting.
answers.barking: Harriers bark moderately with a deep melodious bay that signals excitement or a discovered scent. Their hound heritage drives vocal announcements during pursuits or when spotting movement like squirrels rather than random noise. The sociable temperament means barking often occurs in company with other dogs.
answers.apartment: Harriers do not suit apartment living because their high energy and vocal baying clash with confined indoor routines. The breed needs extensive daily exercise and mental outlets to prevent boredom-driven destruction while their determined wandering instinct requires secure space beyond limited floor area.
answers.first-time: Harriers are not a good first dog because their significant exercise needs and independent prey drive demand experienced handling to curb wandering. The lively determined English hound tests patience with stubbornness on trails making consistent training and boundless stamina management hard for novices.
